questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: English speaking country and that they had courses I was interested in

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: All exchange students were connected with a supervisor. The communication by email was good and they responded fast

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: They showed me where my housing were when i arrived and there were a service desk I could ask for help if needed

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: I lived in a townhouse with three other exchange students. Other options were available as well. At the townhouses we shared a kitchen and bath.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: There were a mandatory meal plan. I choose the minimum one. I paid around 360 CAD a month for this meal plan. Here i ate around 2-3 times a day in the weekdays. I could cook in my kitchen at the townhouse. However, no kitchen tools were there when I arrived.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: I lived with the three other exchange student in a community with only first year students. So the people around you are often much younger than you. However, it was nice that we lived only exchange students together but you don't know who they are before you arrive.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The registration were on their Mobility Online Portal same system as UCPH

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The supervisor were helpful and there was a service desk at campus where you could get help in person

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: It was easy for me to get the courses I wanted. However, once I got there I wanted to change which where a bit more complicated because you get waitlisted until another student drops the course. You have around two weeks in the beginning to change.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Maybe apply for too many courses as a start and show up the first week to see which you like. You will avoid the waitlist then.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I took two really good courses and two less good courses. I find that the quality of the courses vary a lot.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: It is the same as at UCHP, however you should expect more small assignments. Everything you do counts.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The lecture are similar. The tutorials are more about you getting help with the assignments than about the readings.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
ENV201H5 - Enviromental Management
GGR387H5 - Food and Globalization
GGR361H - City planning and development
GGR377 - Introduction to Urban Data anlytics

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
ENV201H5 - Enviromental Management
GGR361H - City planning and development
Both really interesting and the structure where really good

questions.answer: That the natur parks had fees often

questions.answer: I paid more for my housing than expected at first

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were a gym and swimming pool at campus available for students without any extra fees. There were a lot of different drop in sports you could sign up for.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I joined a lot of the yoga classes

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Montreal is a nice city 6 hour away which were nice.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: People were open and helpful so it was easy to talk with people. Everyone around you speaks english with makes it easier as well.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Be open in the beginning of the semester with those you have your courses with. Often people don't know each other in the courses.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: That people are more competitive and they care more about grades than I am used too to an extent were I find it a bit unhealthy

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: That people were curious and helpful - it makes it easier to find connections

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. The tests are handwritten often without notes available 
2. The workload are different because of all the assignments
3. You are not going to Toronto but Mississauga

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: That things often don't go as you planned because you don't know what you will find when you are going to another country

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Using my english skills and because of all the assignments I did practice it a lot. I appreciate the connections I have made with other exchange student and people from Toronto

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The distance between places were hard to get used to and it does not make it easier when the public transport were badly connected

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
